column1: # FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE: Square Enix, Unreal Engine 5.6.1 (SDK MW+EpicGames+UnrealEngine-5_6_1 in main; the desktop renderer, SF_GLSL_SWITCH shaders), SDK 20.5.17, NVN, CRIWARE sound and movies;
# update 1.0.1 (v65536). The card is a Switch 1 cartridge (the game also ships for Switch 2): its secure partition holds the base game, the update and one DLC (a licence only).
# This is the Korean release (title ID 0100B8A026F14000; the Japanese one is 0100606026F12000): the same code as the Japanese one at the same addresses, with the Korean resources, so the
# build ID differs but the addresses below are the Japanese release's. The game's shaders are two IoStore shader library chunks of FFRS-Switch.utoc (type 8) with their 5,919 shader
# groups (type 9), read through the game's own Oodle in the Mac host's tool mode (uepak.py Toc / io_archive / OodleHost, dm/host/hle_oodle.c DM_OODLE_SERVE).
# the on-screen gamepad of the iPhone app: the full layout (D-pad, right stick, L3 / R3) as the other Switch titles
# the card is the Korean release: the game has ko, zh-Hant and zh-Hans
# subsdk0 is NintendoSDK_movie (main imports from it)
# 60 fps (30 on the Switch): the engine's Switch device profile sets rhi.syncinterval=2, so the game asks for present interval 2; the host writes rhi.SyncInterval 1 into its
# console variable (hle_fpslock.c) whenever the game sets it back (at level loads), so the game asks for present interval 1 itself. Unreal steps the game by the time that really
# passed. DM_FPS_TARGET=30 (Documents/env.txt on the iPhone) keeps the game's 30 and saves power.
# Unreal Engine 5.6.1: nninitStartup (main+0x13370) reserves one 62 GB region for the engine (-SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize= in MB up to 4095, game_args below), and its FMallocBinned3
# (38 GB of address space, main+0xae82c: the size 0x980000000 is hardcoded in the game and does not follow -SwitchVirtualAddressSpaceSize=, so that switch cannot help) is
# constructed in place in the bss; the constructor call is cut and the host runs Unreal's heap on a malloc zone (patches.py, hle_uemalloc.c layout UE5_6), and the SDK's node area is
# cut to 62 MB (dm/tools/sdk_patches.py, the SDK build of STEINS;GATE RE:BOOT). The engine hands its region out with a page allocator of its own (main+0x13ef0): a bump pointer, and
# freed blocks kept in free lists by size class, so its address use only grows, and past the region's end OnOutOfMemory (main+0x13c74) aborts. This SDK build aligns regions of
# 2 MB and more to 2 MB only (VammManager::AllocateAddressRegion, sdk+0x145e00), so the region starts right after the node area, in the 5 GB block below, as DRAGON QUEST XI S's.
# the NPDM declares 20 MB of system resource
# the shaders' texture handles: some of them are dynamic (the translator cannot trace them to one slot), the
# game picks them from the c2 tables at run time
# The shaders are Unreal Engine 5's shader libraries in the IoStore container FFRS-Switch.utoc / .ucas: two library chunks (type 8: the engine's global shaders and the game's
# material shaders) with their 5,919 shader groups (type 9). Their tables and groups are Oodle-compressed in two layers, so uepak.py reads them through the game's own decoder in the
# Mac host's tool mode (Toc / io_archive / OodleHost, DM_OODLE_SERVE, served before the SDK starts, no boot) and writes them as version 2 archives; the split reads them as any other.
# Unreal combines a vertex and a pixel shader per draw from its pipeline state, so every vertex shader is made to link with any pixel shader (shader_split.py separable_pairs).
